findings.title: Recovery observes a mutable production project instead of the immutable target
findings.observation: The new reconciliation observes input.productionProject. Its host caller supplies config().composeProject from mutable process environment, even though the attempt and rollback aggregate already bind the immutable target compose project. Stale ROLLING_BACK recovery does not repeat active preflight configuration equality.
findings.trigger: Persist a fresh-attempt aggregate whose production result is lifecycle-null NOT_APPLICABLE for target project A, crash before terminal evidence, recreate an exact-owned resource under A, then retry with a different valid COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME B.
findings.impact: Recovery observes empty B, skips lifecycle completion for NOT_APPLICABLE, writes terminal ROLLED_BACK authority and leaves the exact-owned resource under A. Operators and later lifecycle steps receive false cleanup success.

evidence.description: A temporary exact-head variant of the production-reappearance test removed the lifecycle, persisted the aggregate for idea-validation-prod, recreated its exact-owned container, then changed productionProject before retry. The promise resolved terminalState ROLLED_BACK instead of rejecting with RESOURCE_REAPPEARED. The temporary edit was removed and the tracked diff returned clean.

finalizePersistedRollback passes input.productionProject to reconciliation, while the host active rollback producer supplies config().composeProject from current environment. The aggregate verifier independently binds evidence.composeProject to attempt.target.composeProject but that value is not used for the live observation.

A fresh-context independent reviewer built a separate lifecycle-null recovery regression and reproduced the same false ROLLED_BACK result with one application call, zero additional deletes and the original container still present.
The design and operations contract require re-observation of the exact persisted scope and fail-closed behavior on reappearance or ownership drift.

findings.remediation: Derive the production reconciliation scope from the validated attempt.target.composeProject and persisted evidence.composeProject, or reject any supplied productionProject mismatch before observation. The host active rollback path should pass immutable target authority rather than current configuration.
findings.verification: Add an aggregate-crash regression with lifecycle-null production NOT_APPLICABLE, target project A resource reappearance and current configuration project B. Require one application callback total, zero additional deletes, original resource retained, no terminal evidence or successful lifecycle transition, and a deterministic authority-mismatch failure before observing B.
